Photograph: Dursun Aydemir/Anadolu via Getty Images US news US to levy sanctions against the president and a prosecutor of international criminal court Marco Rubio announced measures against Tomoko Akane and Abdoulaye Seye, who was investigating Israel’s war crimes in Gaza Andrew Roth in Washington Tue 18 Aug 2026 13.50 EDT Last modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 14.11 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The US will sanction the president of the international criminal court (ICC) and a prosecutor tasked with investigating crimes committed by Israel during its war on Gaza. The new sanctions designations were unveiled by Marco Rubio , the US secretary of state, who called the Hague-based ICC a “corrupt and fatally politicized supranational court that has maliciously abused its authority and exceeded its mandate”, in a statement. Rubio announced that the US would sanction Tomoko Akane of Japan, the ICC president, and Abdoulaye Seye of Senegal, an ICC senior trial lawyer, because they had “directly engaged in efforts by the ICC to investigate, arrest, detain, or prosecute officials whose government has not consented to ICC jurisdiction”. The US had previously sanctioned Karim Khan, an ICC prosecutor, who had investigated the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu , and former defense minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes during the Gaza war. Donald Trump in 2025 sanctioned the court, stating in an executive order that it had “engaged in illegitimate and baseless actions targeting America and our close ally Israel”. Rubio did not say specifically which efforts the two ICC officials had engaged in, but Israeli media have reported that Seye is overseeing the investigation into Israeli funding for illegal settlements and the distribution of weapons to settlers in the West Bank . Israeli officials warned local media in May that the ICC may seek five more arrest warrants for ministers and senior military officials involved in violence against Palestinians in the West Bank. https://www.wtxl.com/science-and-tech/an.text: Matt Walker couldn't pet a dog without sneezing — until he and other scientists used a gene editing technique to produce a hypoallergenic beagle named Bailey.Now, he can feed Bailey spoons of peanut butter while she lies on his lap and play fetch with her in Central Park. His allergies didn't go away: Bailey's saliva and hair no longer contain a key allergy-causing protein."The feeling right now is sort of a mix of relief and awe and gratitude that it worked," said Walker, a geneticist. His company, Kindred Companion Sciences, created Bailey and her twin Alfie using a Nobel Prize-winning technique called CRISPR.It'll take years before the millions who suffer from dog-related allergies can walk into a pet store and buy a pooch like Alfie or Bailey.RELATED STORY | Prague zoo keeps polar bears cool with ice cubes as heatwave hitsScientists have to monitor the long-term health effects of the genetic tweak, and find ways to commercialize the approach to make it affordable. And experts not involved with the effort say it could hurt shelter and rescue animals waiting to be adopted."It opens the door to a lot more people being able to own pets. On the negative side, it may discourage people from trying to use strays and unwanted animals that are not engineered to be allergy-free," said bioethicist Arthur Caplan with New York University's Grossman School of Medicine.Researchers have tried to create hypoallergenic pets before, mostly using cloning. But this led to sicker pups that were too genetically similar. Two years ago, researchers used CRISPR to reduce levels of an allergy-causing protein in a cat named Alsik. But it's not yet clear whether this technique is safe to be tested on other cats.Dogs that shed less, like poodles, are often thought of as hypoallergenic. But these pups still produce allergy-causing proteins that end up in their saliva, hair and dander, so they can still make people sniffly.RELATED STORY | Leonardo DiCaprio and Jeff Bezos lead project to save most threatened speciesTo create Alfie and Bailey, scientists started in the lab. They edited the genetic code inside dog skin cells, switching off the main gene responsible for producing allergy-causing proteins. Then they transferred the edited genetic code into eggs that went into a beagle surrogate that gave birth to two healthy female pups in September 2024. Scientists tested their saliva and fur and didn't find signs of the allergy-causing protein.They also performed an allergy test, pricking Walker's skin with extracts from Alfie and Bailey's saliva and dander. His skin reacted to samples from a poodle and goldendoodle, but not from the beagles.The research, published Wednesday in the CRISPR Journal, is the first time such an approach has been tried successfully in dogs.Walker says all dogs have the same allergy-causing gene that was edited in Alfie and Bailey. Kindred Companion Sciences hopes to test the technique on other dogs and service animals to see if they can breed an allergy-free line of pups beyond beagles.Future research should test the gene-edited hypoallergenic dogs on more people with pet allergies to be sure they can soothe symptoms across a broader swath of the human population, said Dr. Jeff SoRelle, a pathologist at University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center.Since the switched-off gene is the main — but not the only — allergy-causing culprit in dogs that was tested, "we don't exactly know just how effective or broadly useful this could be for stopping dog allergy in humans," said SoRelle, who had no role in the study.Bailey lives with Walker in New York, and Alfie lives in Florida with another Kindred scientist. The edit made to their genes is rare but does occur naturally in some dogs, so Walker said it's unlikely to have any negative effects on the pups. But it will still be important to monitor them at routine vet visits and make sure they stay healthy.Walker has had Bailey for a little over a year and says she's become a member of the family.Despite being a lifelong dog lover, his allergies kept him away from pups growing up. Even breeds that were supposed to be more hypoallergenic, like his family's goldendoodle, gave him itchy eyes and painful rashes.But he and Bailey can play tug-of-war together in his living room, and she snuggles at his feet to comfort him when he's sick."It feels just amazing to get to have a dog," Walker said.

Raupelis / LRT Lithuania may seek amendments to the European Unionâs new Migration and Asylum Pact during its 2027 presidency of the EU Council, Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas said Monday, citing concerns about border security and recent migration incidents. âThere are many issues to consider. We will evaluate how the Migration and Asylum Pact is functioning, as it only entered into force on June 12 this year, if I am not mistaken,â Katelynas told reporters at the Lithuanian parliament. The minister said one of the main concerns was that the pact could limit the ability of border authorities to operate effectively at the EUâs external borders. âWe saw this in Spain. However, the Spaniards took measures regardless when facing the tens of thousands who flooded Ceuta,â Katelynas said. He argued that the pact should not prevent EU member states from taking measures to protect their security. Lithuania will therefore assess how the new rules work in practice after it takes over the rotating presidency of the EU Council on January 1, 2027, Katelynas said. âThis is a pressing issue for many member states, particularly those with an external EU border who see these problems and are actively raising them,â he said. After an initial assessment, Lithuania could compile proposals from member states and pass them to Greece, which will hold the EU Council presidency after Lithuania and also faces migration pressure, Katelynas said. The Migration and Asylum Pact entered into force across the EU, including Lithuania, on June 12. The legislation represents a major overhaul of the blocâs common migration policy and is intended to strengthen external border management, improve security and establish a more predictable system for solidarity among member states. Katelynas identified migration policy as one of the key issues Lithuania is likely to address during its EU presidency. His comments came after a recent migration crisis in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, located on Moroccoâs northern coast. Spanish authorities said tens of thousands of people attempted to enter the enclave from Morocco in late July, with more than 100 people reportedly dying during the crossing. Madrid moved to return migrants, and most have since left the enclave. Under the EUâs solidarity mechanism, Lithuania plans to relocate 58 migrants from Cyprus and make a financial contribution of 1.14 million euros. The government has decided to meet its obligations under the pact through a combination of relocation and financial contributions. Beállítom Szerbiában pontosan tudni lehet, mikor indul a vonatközlekedés Belgrád, Budapest és Bécs között: a Szabad Magyar Szó cikke szerint a Budapest–Belgrád-vonalon a december 13-án, az új menetrend életbelépésével lehet először utazni. A portálnak az információt Ljubiša Pejičić, a Srbijavoz állami vasútvállalat megbízott igazgatója is megerősítette. Megkerestük a Közlekedési és Beruházási Minisztériumot, hogy meg tudják-e erősíteni ezt a dátumot, de azt a választ kaptuk, hogy még pár dokumentum hiányzik ahhoz, hogy végleges beindulási dátumokat a magyar fél be tudja jelenteni. A Szabad Magyar Szó cikke szerint a Srbija Voz már most készen áll a járatok elindítására, a magyar fél azonban további ellenőrzéseket kért, mert a vasútvonal magyarországi szakaszán több mint 90 vasúti átjáró van. A szerbiai szakaszon viszont nincsenek szintbeni kereszteződések a közúti forgalommal. A szerb vasútvállalat már azt is közölte, hogy napi nyolc járat indul majd Belgrádból, amelyből hat Budapestig, kettő pedig Bécsig közlekedik. Belgrádtól Budapestig 3 óra lesz az út, Bécsig 6. Ennek legfőbb oka, hogy a vonatok a szerbiai szakaszon óránként akár 200 kilométeres sebességgel is mehetnek, Magyarországon viszont 160 km/óra lesz a legnagyobb megengedett sebesség. Már azt is tudni lehet, hogy mennyibe kerülnek majd a jegyek: a szerb és magyar fővárosok között 35 euróért, Bécsig 43 euróért lehet majd utazni. Vitézy Dávid közlekedési és beruházási miniszter október elején azt írta, október közepére várják a vasútvonal utolsó vizsgálatainak dokumentációját, és ha ezekkel minden rendben van, akkor a magyar szakaszon már október végén indulhatnak vonatok , a nemzetközi közlekedés pedig decemberben indulhat. Cikkünk megjelenése után a minisztérium a Telex kérdésére közölte, a miniszter által október elején elmondottakat fenntartják, végleges beindulási dátumokat csak akkor közölnek, ha minden szükséges dokumentum rendelkezésre áll. A vonal magyarországi szakaszán eredményesen lezajlott a vonatok közlekedését felügyelő irányító rendszernek (egységes európai vonatbefolyásoló rendszer, ETCS) a tesztüzeme, a rendszer üzemszerűen, biztonságosan működött. A teszt kiértékelését a MÁV szakemberei és a hazai közlekedési hatóságok mellett a TÜV minőségbiztosító cég is el fogja végezni, a MÁV saját üzemeltetői bizonyítványa és a TÜV minőségbiztosítási dokumentuma viszont még hiányzik. Ezek kiállítását követően tudja a tárca véglegesíteni a több lépcsőben történő személyszállítás beindításának ütemtervét. Ha mindent rendben találnak, csak akkor indulhat a forgalom.
